To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PM pollution in the urban areas of Zagreb, Budapest and in Sofia is the result of a combination of local emissions, regional and long-range transport, and gas-to-particle transformation of secondary inorganic aerosols.

the most important PM pollution sources and sources of long range transport in the studied cities are: gas-to-particle transformation (sulfate, secondary organic aerosols), primary emissions from biomass combustion and traffic, re-suspended soil (crust) and dust.
